All six items done. Final run: model-gateway lib 1863 passed (baseline 1857), zdr_posture_matrix 6 (6), continue_preconsume_test 8 (7), durable_loop_contract 23 (23, with larger guards and mutation proofs), BFF continue_error_vocabulary 5 (4), SPA contract vitest 49 (43), and `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --keep-going` finished with no errors. I wrote no DB-backed (#[ignore]) tests, so nothing needs the disposable-Postgres harness.

ITEM 1 (done). The spent run-end frames are fixed. `agent_run_failed` and `agent_run_state_unknown` now go through the new `run_end_error_event(request_id, run_id, code, message, spend)`. With the gateway's pre-consume spent they carry retryable false, run_id and approval_spent true. For every other run the frame is the exact `ChatEvent::Error` it was before, retryable true with no run_id or approval_spent. The closed pair is `CONTINUE_SPENT_RUN_END_FRAMES`.
- Tests: the handler-level frame table in tests/continue_preconsume_test.rs gained on/off rows for both frames, so each regime and each frame is covered. A new exact-payload test checks the frames byte for byte. Unit tests in sse.rs pin the unspent form equal to the committed ChatEvent, and that every call site passes `spend`.
- SPA/BFF: a flagged frame was not readable by the existing SPA guards. I added `CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_SPENT_RUN_END_FRAMES` and `chatRunContinueSpentRunEndOf` to the SPA contract (regime 1, flagged frames only). The BFF test `the_spa_run_end_frames_are_the_gateways_and_stay_out_of_the_refusal_lists` pins the SPA pair to the gateway's pair. The existing HTTP and refusal-frame lists are untouched and their parity tests are green.
- Not covered, deferred (item 6): a typed subscription-failure frame and `agent_run_output_unavailable` are still retryable after a spend, as the design said. The same contradiction applies to them.

ITEM 2 (done as a pre-check, not a move). `continue_run` now calls the new `run_agent_request_is_buildable` over the four bearers before the consume, only inside `if resume_enabled`. That is the only local failure `authenticated_run_agent_request` has. If it fails, the answer is `unbuildable_continuation_stream`, a one-frame stream. The frame is `continue_refused` with retryable false, a run_id and no approval_spent.
- Why not move the real construction: it sits inside `agentic_run_stream` after the connected frame, which has 24 parameters shared with ordinary callers. Moving it would mean threading a built request through that signature. The launch still builds the real request and still handles a failure after a spend.
- Test limit: a handler-level test cannot make a verified bearer malformed, because a verified JWT is always valid gRPC metadata, and the `for_test` constructors are cfg(test) of the lib. So the checks are unit tests (pre-check per bearer equals the launch's failure; the refusal stream), a structural order test, and the test below. The "no consume call" part is held by the order test (pre-check inside the switch branch, before the launch closure and before `spawn_consume_then_launch`), not by a consume-counting test.
- Added the behavioural test for a failure after a spend, driven through `agentic_run_stream` directly: connected frame saying spent, then `continue_refused`, no terminalize, nothing published.
- The refusal frame carries no approval_spent, so the SPA reads it as regime 2 (spend unknown). That is conservative; the gateway knows nothing was spent.

ITEM 3 (done). Added Unauthenticated and zero-retention-trailer rows with the switch on and off. The trailer rides FailedPrecondition, and also PermissionDenied: on gives `durable_mutation_forbidden`, off follows the committed confirmed-rejection arm. The construction-failure-after-spend test is the one above.

ITEM 4 (done), each with a mutation proof.
- (a) `resume_pair_violations` now accepts the plain `&& replay_is_fenced` read only inside an `if !( .. )` refusal condition. The negated read is allowed only as the warn line's own `if` (`continue_replay_refused_ledger_off`) nested in that refusal body. An inverted accept, a negated read elsewhere, and an accept written as a positive `if` are all flagged; a missing plain read is flagged too.
- (b) `gateway_consume_violations` now requires `omit_call: true` inside the one ConsumeApprovalRequest literal. Dropping the line from `preconsume_request` while a rogue `omit_call: true` survives elsewhere is now red.
- (c) I guarded the second `writer_gate` call in `restore_continuation`. Its shape must be exactly `(req, route, runtime_loop::effect::ledger_enabled(), 0, true, true)`, with exactly two production calls (that one and run_rounds). The guard comment says why each literal is right. Mutations: depth 1, ledger `true`, release false, in-place false, 5 arguments, a third call, call removed.
- (d) `no_attestation_violations` takes a third argument. `attestation_sources()` scans the Go tree (generated bindings and hand-written Go), the BFF `apps/gateway/src` and the SPA `src`, with comments stripped. Test files and dependency directories are skipped, each tree has a minimum file count, and the check folds casing and underscores. Mutations: a Go struct field, a Go getter, a BFF field, SPA .ts and .tsx, and a camelCase Rust variant. Quiet comments stay green.
- I ran the new mutations against a copy of the committed guards, and every one of them (a, b, c and d) passed with no violations. The new guards catch them.

ITEM 5 (done). The doc comment now sits on `ConsumeOnlyServer` and `ServerBehaviour` has its own. Stale sentences fixed in the mp-contracts `LOOP_RESUME_ENV` rustdoc, the execution-core compose comment and the sse.rs test header (plus one "will own" comment).

ITEM 6 (recorded, no code): see the deferred ledger text.

Production mutation checks, each restored with cp and verified by cmp and sha256 (sse.rs unchanged from the verified version):
- retryable forced true on a spent run-end frame: red in the lib test and in two handler tests.
- early return after a spend removed: red in the behavioural test (`session_terminalization_failed` instead of `continue_refused`).
- zero-retention branch disabled in classify: red on the on / zero-retention row.
- Unauthenticated dropped from the confirmed-rejection arm: red on the off / Unauthenticated row.
- Before the pre-check existed, the structural test was red.

No cargo transient failures (LNK1104 or other-unit breakage) were hit. The only transient was a vitest worker-start timeout on the first run; the retry passed.

### Addendum to the 2026-10-18 entry (WS03 S7c hardening, 2026-10-19)

**Heading is stale.** The entry is titled "... S7c-B gateway wiring still to land"; the wiring has landed (commit 8c32988a, tests in tests/continue_preconsume_test.rs). Retitle it "... S7c-B gateway wiring landed".

**Spent continuations: every failure frame is final.** With the gateway's pre-consume spent, the two frames that follow the executor's ANSWER, `agent_run_failed` and `agent_run_state_unknown`, now carry `retryable: false`, the run id and `approval_spent: true` (sse.rs `run_end_error_event`, closed pair `CONTINUE_SPENT_RUN_END_FRAMES`). This resolves the contradiction between the design invariant (every failure frame of a spent continuation is final) and approach E (post-response frames keep their committed values) in favour of the invariant, for SPENT continuations only. For every other run the two frames are byte-identical to the committed ones. The SPA reads the flagged form through `chatRunContinueSpentRunEndOf` (regime 1); unflagged they are regime 3 and read by no continue guard. The SPA pair and the gateway pair are pinned equal by apps/gateway/tests/continue_error_vocabulary.rs.

**Still open (follow-up, not in this change).** Two more post-response frames of a spent continuation are still retryable: the typed subscription-failure frames and `agent_run_output_unavailable`. They have the same contradiction. Proposed resolution: same treatment through `run_end_error_event`, widening the closed pair to three codes and the SPA/BFF pair with it.

**A request that cannot be built is refused before the consume.** With the resume switch on, `continue_run` checks the RunAgent request's credentials (`run_agent_request_is_buildable`, the one local failure `authenticated_run_agent_request` has) BEFORE the gateway spends the click. A failure answers HTTP 200 with a one-frame stream: `continue_refused`, not retryable, naming the run, WITHOUT `approval_spent` (nothing spent, nothing sent). The SPA reads that frame as regime 2 (spend unknown), which is conservative: the approval is still usable. The real request is still built later in agentic_run_stream, and a failure there after a spend stays `continue_refused` with `approval_spent: true`, no terminalization and no degraded event, until the renewed recovery window ends the run. With the switch off nothing changes. A verified bearer is always valid gRPC metadata, so the pre-check is defence in depth, not a reachable path today.

**Metrics consequence, recorded (WS03 S7c, no code).** RUN_STARTED is published before the dispatch result. A refused continuation therefore shows a started run with no closing event, until session-core recovery terminalizes it about 15 minutes after the spend (the renewed recovery window of the spend-only consume). This is a consequence of the design, not a bug: the gateway never terminalizes a spent continuation, because a refusal can be continuation_already_consumed while another segment is live. Dashboards that count started-without-closed runs will show these for up to 15 minutes.

**Guards tightened (durable_loop_contract.rs).** The same-claim replay accept is now read in its one real shape (plain `&& replay_is_fenced` inside the `if !( .. )` refusal; the negated read only as the warn line inside it), so an inverted accept (accepted only with the ledger OFF) is red. `omit_call: true` must be a field OF the one ConsumeApprovalRequest literal. The in-place resume's own writer gate (restore_continuation) is read as `(req, route, ledger_enabled(), 0, true, true)` with exactly two production writer_gate calls. The no-attestation scan (`consumed_by_gateway`, any casing) now covers the generated Go bindings, the BFF and the SPA.

A failure answers HTTP 200 with a one-frame stream: `continue_refused`, not retryable, naming the run, WITHOUT `approval_spent` (nothing spent, nothing sent). The SPA reads that frame as regime 2 (spend unknown), which is conservative: the approval is still usable. The real request is still built later in agentic_run_stream, and a failure there after a spend stays `continue_refused` with `approval_spent: true`, no terminalization and no degraded event, until the renewed recovery window ends the run. With the switch off nothing changes. A verified bearer is always valid gRPC metadata, so the pre-check is defence in depth, not a reachable path today.

**Metrics consequence, recorded (WS03 S7c, no code).** RUN_STARTED is published before the dispatch result. A refused continuation therefore shows a started run with no closing event, until session-core recovery terminalizes it about 15 minutes after the spend (the renewed recovery window of the spend-only consume). This is a consequence of the design, not a bug: the gateway never terminalizes a spent continuation, because a refusal can be continuation_already_consumed while another segment is live. Dashboards that count started-without-closed runs will show these for up to 15 minutes.

**Guards tightened (durable_loop_contract.rs).** The same-claim replay accept is now read in its one real shape (plain `&& replay_is_fenced` inside the `if !( .. )` refusal; the negated read only as the warn line inside it), so an inverted accept (accepted only with the ledger OFF) is red. `omit_call: true` must be a field OF the one ConsumeApprovalRequest literal. The in-place resume's own writer gate (restore_continuation) is read as `(req, route, ledger_enabled(), 0, true, true)` with exactly two production writer_gate calls. The no-attestation scan (`consumed_by_gateway`, any casing) now covers the generated Go bindings, the BFF and the SPA.

A client that follows `retryable` re-posts the continue and gets 409 continuation_already_consumed. The SPA contract does not read it either, so it falls to the generic retryable regime. findings.issue: Item 4(a) is only partly met. The new resume_pair_violations still accepts an inverted accept if it is spelled any way other than `&& !replay_is_fenced`. The regex `^\.\s*same_claim\s*&&\s*(!?)\s*replay_is_fenced\b` reads one token. It classes `consumed.same_claim && replay_is_fenced == false` (or `!= true`) as the plain read. That read sits inside the `if !( .. ) { .. continuation_already_consumed .. }` condition, so the guard passes it. A disjunct that does not touch `.same_claim` at all, such as `|| (consumed.already_consumed && !replay_is_fenced)` added inside the refusal's `!( .. )`, accepts every consumed approval when the ledger is off, and the guard never looks at it.
findings.evidence: resume_pair_violations: `followed.captures(..)`, then `shape[1].is_empty()` marks a plain read, and `enclosing_if` only checks `condition.starts_with('!') && body.contains("continuation_already_consumed")`. Nothing checks what the rest of the refusal condition says. agent.rs:5891-5892 is `if !(consumed.consumed || (consumed.already_consumed && consumed.same_claim && replay_is_fenced))`. Both rewrites above leave the guard green (worked out by hand against the guard code; not run, because review mode allows no file edits). Mitigation: the behavioural tests a_same_claim_replay_is_refused_when_the_ledger_is_off and a_same_claim_replay_with_the_ledger_off_logs_and_refuses_as_before in agent.rs would still go red.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the refusal condition's whole shape. Squash it and compare it with `!(consumed.consumed || (consumed.already_consumed && consumed.same_claim && replay_is_fenced))`, or require that `replay_is_fenced` appears inside the `!( .. )` exactly once, unnegated and not compared. Add must_flag mutations for `replay_is_fenced == false` and for an extra `|| !replay_is_fenced` disjunct.

findings.issue: Item 2 was built as a pre-check that cannot be reached today, and its answer is weaker than what the gateway knows. When run_agent_request_is_buildable fails, the route answers HTTP 200 with a lone `continue_refused` frame: no `connected` frame and no `approval_spent`. The SPA contract reads that as regime 2 (spend unknown, follow the run). The gateway knows nothing was spent, and the failure is deterministic, so a retry hits it again. The route already has an HTTP path for refusals that cannot follow a consume, read as spend `no` (CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_PRE_CONSUME_ONLY_HTTP_REFUSALS, and the 401 `missing_bearer` earlier in the same handler). Also, 'no consume call' is proved only by continue_run_checks_the_request_before_it_consumes, which asserts the order of the source text, not behaviour. The design asked for a test showing no consume call. The implementer did report this deviation.
findings.evidence: continue_run: `if resume_enabled { if let Err(error) = run_agent_request_is_buildable(..) { ..; return Ok(unbuildable_continuation_stream(&run_id)); } }`. unbuildable_continuation_stream calls continue_refusal_event(.., ApprovalSpend::NotSpent). The test uses position(&body, "run_agent_request_is_buildable(") < position(&body, "spawn_consume_then_launch(").
findings.suggested_fix: Answer the pre-check failure as an HTTP refusal that cannot follow a consume. Reuse `Err(continue_error(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, "missing_bearer"))`, whose SPA effect is already defined. Or record in the SPA contract that this `continue_refused` is pre-consume. Behaviour can be tested with a lib-level test that drives the pre-check branch with a counting ApprovalConsumer, since for_test bearers are available in the lib tests.
